records.source: ה֤וֹי כָּל־צָמֵא֙ לְכ֣וּ לַמַּ֔יִם וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵֽין־ל֖וֹ כָּ֑סֶף לְכ֤וּ שִׁבְרוּ֙ וֶֽאֱכֹ֔לוּ וּלְכ֣וּ שִׁבְר֗וּ בְּלוֹא־כֶ֛סֶף וּבְל֥וֹא מְחִ֖יר יַ֥יִן וְחָלָֽב׃
records.gloss: Ho, every thirsty [one], come to the waters; and [the one] who has no money, come, buy grain and eat; and come, buy grain without money and without price, wine and milk.
pieces: Listen, all who thirst: come down to the water! \q You who have no silver, \q come, buy grain and eat. \q Come, buy grain, wine and milk, and pay nothing for them.

L.1: Ho, every thirsty [one], come to the waters; \q and [you] who have no silver, \q come, buy grain and eat! \q Come, buy grain without silver and without price, wine and milk!

R.1: Listen! Is anyone thirsty? Come and drink the water. \q Do you have no money? \q Come anyway. Get food and eat it. \q Come and get wine and milk. You do not have to pay anything for them.

decisions.choice: ho: a call for attention, here an invitation
decisions.reason: The same cry usually opens a warning of doom ("woe", 5:8; 10:1). Here it calls out like a seller in the market or a host at a door, and is followed by "come" three times. Zechariah 2:10 uses it the same way to call exiles home.

decisions.choice: buy grain: buy food
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for grain and is used of buying food (Genesis 42:2-3). The paradox of buying without money says that what God gives cannot be paid for.

decisions.choice: water, wine and milk offered free: God's invitation to a banquet
decisions.reason: Wisdom invites the simple to her meal in Proverbs 9:5. Jesus calls the thirsty to come to him and drink (John 7:37), and Revelation 22:17 echoes this verse: whoever is thirsty may take the water of life without cost.

decisions.choice: Listen
decisions.reason: The interjection is an invitation here (m1), so Balanced and Readable use a call to attention rather than an old-fashioned cry.

decisions.choice: Is anyone thirsty? Do you have no money?
decisions.reason: Readable turns the descriptions of the hearers into short questions, as a caller in the street would.

records.heading: Free food and drink for all who thirst

records.source: לָ֤מָּה תִשְׁקְלוּ־כֶ֨סֶף֙ בְּֽלוֹא־לֶ֔חֶם וִיגִיעֲכֶ֖ם בְּל֣וֹא לְשָׂבְעָ֑ה שִׁמְע֨וּ שָׁמ֤וֹעַ אֵלַי֙ וְאִכְלוּ־ט֔וֹב וְתִתְעַנַּ֥ג בַּדֶּ֖שֶׁן נַפְשְׁכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Why do you weigh out money for not bread, and your toil for not satisfaction? Listen carefully to me, and eat good, and let delight itself in fatness your appetite.
pieces: Why pay out silver for what is not bread, \q and the fruit of your work for what never fills you? \q Pay close attention to me: eat what is good, \q and let your appetite delight in the finest food.

L.2: Why do you weigh out silver for [what is] not bread, \q and your labor for [what does] not satisfy? \q Listen carefully to me, and eat [what is] good, \q and let your soul delight itself in fatness.

R.2: Why spend your money on things that are not real food? \q Why work hard for things that do not fill you up? \q Listen to me carefully. Then you will eat what is good, \q and you will enjoy the best food there is.

decisions.choice: weigh out silver: pay
decisions.reason: Before coins were common, silver was weighed on scales to make a payment (Genesis 23:16; Jeremiah 32:9-10).

decisions.choice: listen carefully: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: The command is followed by the infinitive of the same verb, which strengthens it: listen and keep listening.

decisions.choice: fatness: rich food; your soul: your appetite, your whole self
decisions.reason: Fat was the richest part of a meal and stands for the best food (25:6; Psalm 63:6). The word often translated "soul" also means appetite and the living self (5:14; 29:8).

decisions.choice: the fruit of your work
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "your toil" as what toil earns, the wages spent in the first line.

records.source: הַטּ֤וּ אָזְנְכֶם֙ וּלְכ֣וּ אֵלַ֔י שִׁמְע֖וּ וּתְחִ֣י נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם וְאֶכְרְתָ֤ה לָכֶם֙ בְּרִ֣ית עוֹלָ֔ם חַֽסְדֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד הַנֶּאֱמָנִֽים׃
records.gloss: Incline your ear and come to me; listen, and let live your soul; and I will cut for you a covenant of perpetuity, the loyal loves of David, the sure [ones].
pieces: Turn your ears this way and come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q hear me, and you will truly live. \q I will grant you a covenant that stands forever: \q the loyal love I pledged to David, which does not fail.

L.3: Incline your ear and come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q listen, and your soul will live; \q and I will make with you an everlasting covenant, \q the sure acts of loyal love [to] David.

R.3: Pay attention and come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q Listen to me, and you will live. \q I will make a covenant with you, a promise that will last forever. \q I will show you the same faithful love that I promised to David, a love that never fails.

decisions.choice: the sure loyal love of David: the faithful promises God made to David
decisions.reason: God promised David a lasting house and throne and swore that his loyal love would not be taken from him (2 Samuel 7:12-16; Psalm 89:2-5, 29-38). Here those promises are opened to the whole people. The phrase may also mean the faithful deeds David himself did, but the promises fit the setting of a covenant better.

decisions.choice: quoted in Acts 13:34
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this line in its Greek form ("the holy and sure things of David") to say that God raised Jesus from the dead and will not let him decay.

decisions.choice: I will make an everlasting covenant: literally "cut a covenant"
decisions.reason: A covenant was "cut", perhaps from the animals cut in two at its making (Genesis 15:9-18; Jeremiah 34:18). The everlasting covenant is also promised in 61:8.

decisions.choice: a promise that will last forever
decisions.reason: Readable explains a covenant as a binding promise, as in 54:10.

records.source: הֵ֛ן עֵ֥ד לְאוּמִּ֖ים נְתַתִּ֑יו נָגִ֥יד וּמְצַוֵּ֖ה לְאֻמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Here, a witness [to] peoples I made him, a leader and commander [of] peoples.
pieces: Look: I set him up as a witness to the peoples, \q a prince who gave orders to nations.

L.4: Look, a witness [to] peoples I made him, \q a leader and commander [of] peoples.

R.4: Think of David. I made him {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witness to the nations. \q I made him a leader who commanded many peoples.

decisions.choice: him: David, whom God made a witness to the nations
alternatives: the coming king from David's line
decisions.reason: David's victories and songs made the LORD known among foreign peoples (2 Samuel 22:44-50; Psalm 18:44-50). The line may also look ahead to a coming king from David's line (Jeremiah 30:9; Ezekiel 34:23-24).

decisions.choice: leader: the ruler God appoints over his people
decisions.reason: The word is used of Saul and David as rulers chosen by God (1 Samuel 13:14; 2 Samuel 7:8).

decisions.choice: Think of David
decisions.reason: Readable names the person meant by "him" (m1), from verse 3.

records.source: הֵ֣ן גּ֤וֹי לֹֽא־תֵדַע֙ תִּקְרָ֔א וְג֥וֹי לֹֽא־יְדָע֖וּךָ אֵלֶ֣יךָ יָר֑וּצוּ לְמַ֨עַן֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וְלִקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֥י פֵאֲרָֽךְ׃ס
records.gloss: Here, a nation [that] not you know you will call, and a nation [that] not knew you to you will run, on account of Yahweh your God and for the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you.
pieces: You in turn will summon a nation you have never known, \q and a nation that never knew you will hurry to you, \q drawn by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q the Holy One of Israel, who has made you shine with honor.

L.5: Look, a nation [that] you do not know you will call, \q and a nation [that] has not known you will run to you, \q because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q and for the Holy One of Israel, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made you beautiful.

R.5: In the same way, you will call nations that you do not know. \q Nations that do not know you will come running to you. \q They will come because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q the Holy One of Israel. He has given you honor.

decisions.choice: you: the people of Israel, who take up David's role
alternatives: the coming king from David's line
decisions.reason: The pronoun is masculine singular. After verse 4 it is the people addressed in verses 1-3, who now call nations as David once ruled them. Some take it as the coming king.

decisions.choice: he has glorified you: given you beauty and honor
decisions.reason: The verb means to adorn or make beautiful. The same words close 60:9, where the nations come to Zion for the same reason.

decisions.choice: a nation: any nation, so nations in general
decisions.reason: The singular stands for nations of every kind, as the parallel lines show.

decisions.choice: In the same way
decisions.reason: Readable links Israel's call to the nations with David's role in verse 4, which "look" introduces.

records.source: דִּרְשׁ֥וּ יְהוָ֖ה בְּהִמָּצְא֑וֹ קְרָאֻ֖הוּ בִּֽהְיוֹת֥וֹ קָרֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: Seek Yahweh while he lets himself be found; call on him while he is near.
pieces: Look for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can still be found; \q call to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is close by.

L.6: Seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lets {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} be found; \q call on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is near.

R.6: Turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} now, while you can still find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q Pray to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} now, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is near.

decisions.choice: while he lets himself be found: the time to seek him is now
decisions.reason: The verb form means "let himself be found". The line implies a time of opportunity that should not be missed (Deuteronomy 4:29; Jeremiah 29:13-14; Psalm 32:6).

decisions.choice: seek, call on: turn to God in worship and prayer
decisions.reason: To seek the LORD is to turn to him and live by his word (Amos 5:4-6); to call on him is to pray to him by name.

decisions.choice: now
decisions.reason: Readable states the urgency that "while" implies (m1).

records.heading: A call to return, and a word that does its work

records.source: יַעֲזֹ֤ב רָשָׁע֙ דַּרְכּ֔וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אָ֖וֶן מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֑יו וְיָשֹׁ֤ב אֶל־יְהוָה֙ וִֽירַחֲמֵ֔הוּ וְאֶל־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ כִּֽי־יַרְבֶּ֥ה לִסְלֽוֹחַ׃
records.gloss: Let forsake [the] wicked his way, and [the] man of wickedness his thoughts, and let him return to Yahweh, that he may have compassion on him, and to our God, for he will increase to forgive.
pieces: Let those who do wrong leave their path behind, \q and the evil their schemes. \q Let them come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will show them mercy; \q let them come back to our God, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is generous to forgive.

L.7: Let [the] wicked [one] abandon his way, \q and [the] {{gender:person|man}} of evil his thoughts; \q and let him turn back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will have compassion on him, \q and to our God, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will multiply to forgive.

R.7: Wicked people must stop doing evil. \q They must stop planning to do wrong. \q They must come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be kind to them. \q They must turn to our God, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will forgive them completely.

decisions.choice: way and thoughts: how a person lives and what a person plans
decisions.reason: The two words return in verses 8-9, where God's ways and thoughts are set against human ones.

decisions.choice: return: turn back to God, repent
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual word for repentance, a people's return to their covenant God (Deuteronomy 30:2-3; Isaiah 44:22).

decisions.choice: he will multiply to forgive: he forgives fully and freely
decisions.reason: The verb "increase" with "to forgive" means forgiving abundantly. Verses 8-9 give the reason: his ways are not human ways.

decisions.choice: those who do wrong; wicked people
decisions.reason: The singular "the wicked" and "the man" stand for anyone of that kind, so Balanced and Readable use plurals that include everyone.

records.source: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א מַחְשְׁבוֹתַי֙ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א דַרְכֵיכֶ֖ם דְּרָכָ֑י נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: For not my thoughts [are] your thoughts, and not your ways [are] my ways, utterance of Yahweh.
pieces: What I plan is not what you plan, \q and the paths you take are not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} paths, \q declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.8: For not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} thoughts [are] your thoughts, \q and not your ways [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways, \q declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.8: I do not think the way you think. \q You do not act the way I act. \q This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says.

decisions.choice: for: the reason God forgives so freely
decisions.reason: The verse explains verse 7. People do not forgive as freely as God does, because his thoughts and ways are not like theirs.

decisions.choice: thoughts and ways: plans and actions
decisions.reason: The pair picks up verse 7, where the wicked must give up their way and their thoughts.

records.source: כִּֽי־גָבְה֥וּ שָׁמַ֖יִם מֵאָ֑רֶץ כֵּ֣ן גָּבְה֤וּ דְרָכַי֙ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֔ם וּמַחְשְׁבֹתַ֖י מִמַּחְשְׁבֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: For they are high [the] heavens above [the] earth, so they are high my ways above your ways, and my thoughts above your thoughts.
pieces: As far as the heavens tower over the earth, \q so far do {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways tower over yours, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} thoughts over yours.

L.9: For [as] high [as the] heavens are above [the] earth, \q so high are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways above your ways, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} thoughts above your thoughts.

R.9: The sky is far above the earth. \q In the same way, the way I do things is far above the way you do things. \q My thoughts are far above your thoughts.

decisions.choice: as high as the heavens: God's ways are greater, above all in mercy
decisions.reason: The distance is not only that God is hard to understand. In the setting of verse 7 it is the size of his mercy, as in Psalm 103:11, where his loyal love is as high as the heavens are above the earth.

decisions.choice: for the heavens are high: the comparison is implied in the standard Hebrew text
alternatives: for as the heavens are high
decisions.reason: The standard text has no word for "as"; the comparison is clear from "so" in the next line. The Great Isaiah Scroll is reported to read "for as the heavens are high", which gives the same sense.

records.source: כִּ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵרֵד֩ הַגֶּ֨שֶׁם וְהַשֶּׁ֜לֶג מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם וְשָׁ֨מָּה֙ לֹ֣א יָשׁ֔וּב כִּ֚י אִם־הִרְוָ֣ה אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהוֹלִידָ֖הּ וְהִצְמִיחָ֑הּ וְנָ֤תַן זֶ֨רַע֙ לַזֹּרֵ֔עַ וְלֶ֖חֶם לָאֹכֵֽל׃
records.gloss: For just as comes down the rain and the snow from the heavens, and there not it returns, unless it has watered the earth and made it bring forth and made it sprout, and given seed to the sower and bread to the eater,
pieces: Just as rain and snow fall from the heavens and do not go back up \q until they have soaked the ground \q and made it bud and grow, \q giving seed to the one who sows \q and bread to the one who eats,

L.10: For just as the rain and the snow come down from the heavens and do not return there \q unless they have watered the earth \q and made it bear and sprout, \q and given seed to the sower \q and bread to the eater,

R.10: Rain and snow fall from the sky. They do not go back up into the sky until they have watered the ground. \q They make the plants grow and produce grain. \q Then farmers have seed to plant, \q and people have bread to eat.

decisions.choice: just as: the first half of a comparison completed in verse 11
decisions.reason: Verses 10 and 11 are one sentence: as the rain does its work before it returns, so does God's word.

decisions.choice: unless: the rain does not go back without first doing its work
decisions.reason: The two words together mean "but rather" or "until" after a negative. The same phrase returns in verse 11.

decisions.choice: rain and snow: the winter moisture on which the year's crops depend
decisions.reason: In the land of Israel the rain comes in the winter months, and the harvest depends on it (Deuteronomy 11:14). Snow falls on the high ground.

decisions.choice: separate sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long comparison into short sentences and joins it to verse 11 with "My word is like that".

records.source: כֵּ֣ן יִֽהְיֶ֤ה דְבָרִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵצֵ֣א מִפִּ֔י לֹֽא־יָשׁ֥וּב אֵלַ֖י רֵיקָ֑ם כִּ֤י אִם־עָשָׂה֙ אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפַ֔צְתִּי וְהִצְלִ֖יחַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שְׁלַחְתִּֽיו׃
records.gloss: so is my word which goes out from my mouth; not it will return to me empty, unless it has done that which I desired and has succeeded [in that for] which I sent it.
pieces: so it is with the word that leaves {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth: \q it will not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with nothing done, \q but it will do what I want \q and succeed in the errand I sent it on.

L.11: so will {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word be that goes out from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth: \q it will not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} empty, \q unless it has done what I desired \q and succeeded [in that for] which I sent it.

R.11: My word is like that. \q When I speak, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word does not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} without results. \q It does what I want it to do. \q It succeeds in the work I send it to do.

decisions.choice: my word: what God says, his promise and command
decisions.reason: God's word stands forever (40:8) and carries out what he says (44:26; 45:23). Here it is pictured as a messenger he sends out (Psalm 107:20; 147:15).

decisions.choice: empty: empty-handed, without having done its task
decisions.reason: The word is used of someone who goes or comes back with nothing in hand (Genesis 31:42; Ruth 1:21).

decisions.choice: succeeded: carried its task through
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 53:10, where the will of the LORD succeeds in the servant's hand.

records.source: כִּֽי־בְשִׂמְחָ֣ה תֵצֵ֔אוּ וּבְשָׁל֖וֹם תּֽוּבָל֑וּן הֶהָרִ֣ים וְהַגְּבָע֗וֹת יִפְצְח֤וּ לִפְנֵיכֶם֙ רִנָּ֔ה וְכָל־עֲצֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה יִמְחֲאוּ־כָֽף׃
records.gloss: For in joy you will go out, and in peace you will be led; the mountains and the hills will break forth before you [in] a shout of joy, and all the trees of the field will clap [the] palm.
pieces: You will set out with gladness \q and be guided along in peace. \q Mountains and hills will ring with shouts of joy ahead of you, \q and every tree in the fields will clap its hands.

L.12: For in joy you will go out, \q and in peace you will be led; \q the mountains and the hills will burst out before you [with] a ringing cry, \q and all the trees of the field will clap [the] palm.

R.12: You will leave Babylon with joy. \q God will lead you out in peace. \q It will be as if the mountains and hills burst into happy songs as you go by. \q It will be as if all the trees in the fields clap their hands.

decisions.choice: you will go out and be led: a new exodus from exile
decisions.reason: The words recall the call to leave Babylon (48:20; 52:11-12) and the way God led Israel out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: the mountains sing and the trees clap: creation joins the celebration
decisions.reason: Isaiah pictures the whole creation rejoicing at what God does for his people (44:23; 49:13). Psalm 98:8 has the rivers clap their hands.

decisions.choice: leave Babylon; God will lead you
decisions.reason: Readable names the place left (m1) and the one who leads, which the passive verb leaves unstated.

decisions.choice: It will be as if
decisions.reason: Readable marks the singing mountains and clapping trees as a picture.

records.source: תַּ֤חַת הַֽנַּעֲצוּץ֙ יַעֲלֶ֣ה בְר֔וֹשׁ וְתַ֥חַת הַסִּרְפַּ֖ד יַעֲלֶ֣ה הֲדַ֑ס וְהָיָ֤ה לַֽיהוָה֙ לְשֵׁ֔ם לְא֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת׃ס
records.gloss: In place of the thornbush will grow up [the] cypress, and in place of the nettle will grow up [the] myrtle; and it will be to Yahweh for a name, for a sign of perpetuity [that] not will be cut off.
pieces: Where thornbushes grew, cypress trees will rise; \q where nettles grew, myrtle will spring up. \q This will win {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a name, \q a sign that will last forever and never be cut down.

L.13: Instead of the thornbush the cypress will come up, \q and instead of the nettle the myrtle will come up; \q and it will be to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for a name, \q for a sign of perpetuity [that] will not be cut off.

R.13: Tall cypress trees will grow where thornbushes grew. \q Myrtle trees will grow where weeds grew. \q This will make people honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q It will be a sign that lasts forever and is never destroyed.

decisions.choice: thornbush, cypress, nettle, myrtle: plants whose exact kinds are uncertain
decisions.reason: The first word is a thorny shrub (7:19). The third appears only here and names some weed or brier. The tall tree may be a cypress, juniper or fir, and the myrtle is a fragrant evergreen shrub (41:19).

decisions.choice: it will be to the LORD for a name: it will win him renown
decisions.reason: A name is a reputation. What God does for his people makes his name known (63:12, 14; Jeremiah 13:11).

decisions.choice: trees instead of thorns: the curse of the land reversed
decisions.reason: Thorns and briers stand for land under judgment (Genesis 3:18; Isaiah 5:6; 7:23-25; 32:13). Here they give way to fine trees.

decisions.choice: weeds
decisions.reason: Readable uses a general word for a plant that cannot be identified with certainty (m1).
